articles.title: Peter Thiel Decamps To Argentina: What Does It Mean For JD Vance's Chances To Win The 2028 Election?
articles.teaser: Peter Thiel decamped to Argentina as VP JD Vance's 2028 Polymarket odds slipped to 18%, but Palantir (PLTR) may gain on Milei surveillance contracts.
articles.body:
Peter Thiel reportedly bought a $12 million mansion in the Barrio Parque enclave of Buenos Aires and temporarily relocated his family to Argentina.

The decision was driven by concerns about the United States, particularly a proposed 5% wealth tax on California billionaires heading to November’s ballot.

The New York Times reported Thursday that Thiel has met repeatedly with Argentine President Javier Milei and hosted a candlelit dinner with Argentine economists where the conversation turned to the Antichrist, a subject Thiel returns to in lectures.

Argentina has reportedly explored offering him citizenship.

Vance Loses His Patron

Thiel is the long-time political backer of Vice President JD Vance, having staked $15 million on Vance’s 2022 Ohio Senate run. That was the largest single-candidate donation Thiel had ever made.

The move comes as prediction markets cool sharply on Vance’s 2028 presidential prospects.

On Polymarket, Vance’s odds to win the 2028 presidential election sit at 18.4%, down from a peak near 31% in December 2025. The decline accelerated after the US-Israel-Iran conflict broke out on February 28.

His odds to win the Republican nomination have trended downwards, but traders still treat him as the GOP frontrunner, at 33%.

A separate market on Vance leaving the vice presidency by year-end sits at 9%.

Rubio Closes The Gap

Vance’s main rival, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is widely credited with being instrumental in the January raid that captured Nicolás Maduro and the subsequent Venezuela transition.

He stands in sharp contrast to the isolationist Vance, whose America First instincts have reportedly been sidelined by Trump on the major foreign policy decisions of 2026.

Trump publicly acknowledged Vance was “philosophically a little bit different” on Operation Epic Fury, the US-Israel war against Iran launched February 28. Politico reported Vance privately opposed the strikes through back channels.

On Kalshi, Rubio holds better odds than Vance to win the 2028 election, a notable divergence from Polymarket. California Governor Gavin Newsom leads the Democratic field at 23% on Polymarket, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is second with 11%.

The Palantir Trade Cuts Both Ways

The Thiel-Vance complex has a clean equity proxy in Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR), the data analytics firm Thiel co-founded. Thiel and Vance also co-invested in Rumble (NASDAQ:RUM) in 2021.

Thiel’s relocation may expand Palantir’s hemispheric footprint rather than shrink it. Argentine officials have reportedly been discussing potential Palantir integrations with state intelligence agencies, according to local media coverage of Thiel’s visit to Buenos Aires.

articles.title: Palantir Stock Is Either A Bargain Or A Bubble, Depending On Who You Ask
articles.teaser: Two analysts read the same earnings report and reached conclusions $140 apart, reflecting the disagreement about Palantir's value.
articles.body:
Two analysts read the same earnings report on the same day and reached conclusions $140 apart. 

That is the current state of Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) on Wall Street, and says almost everything about how the market is pricing AI software right now.

  • PLTR stock is climbing. See the chart and price action here. 

On May 5, after Palantir posted its first-quarter results, RBC Capital reiterated an Underperform rating with a $90 price target. 

Hours later, Wedbush’s Dan Ives reiterated an Outperform with a $230 target.

That $140 spread — more than 150% of the bear case target — is not a disagreement about the quarter. Both firms saw the same numbers. 

Read Also: SentinelOne Stock Craters After Q1 Results — Here's Why

It is a disagreement about what Palantir fundamentally is, and what it is worth.

According to Benzinga's data, the consensus rating is Buy, with an average target of $173.76 across 29 analysts — but that average masks the chaos underneath. 

Citigroup and Rosenblatt both carry $225 targets. DA Davidson just cut to Neutral at $165. HSBC downgraded to Hold on May 1 with a $151 target. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley sit at Neutral, the “we genuinely don’t know” camp, and it is a crowded one.

The Bull Case

The bull case, championed most loudly by Ives — who has called Palantir the “Messi of AI” and expects it to join the trillion-dollar market-cap club — rests on the idea that Palantir’s AIP platform represents a uniquely defensible software layer. 

Government contracts provide durable revenue. The commercial business is accelerating. No one else has built what Palantir has built.

Read Also: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock Jumps After Dell's Massive Q1 Beat On AI Demand

The Bear Case

The bear case is simpler: Palantir stock trades at 161 times trailing earnings and 98 times forward estimates, per Benzinga Pro data. 

At those multiples, the valuation prices in years of flawless execution, and any stumble in sentiment or growth — the kind that has hurt high-multiple software names before — could compress the multiple fast. 

Bears also point to persistently high stock-based compensation as a drag on real profitability.

The $140 Question

The next real test comes with second-quarter earnings in August. Revenue growth trajectory and any update on AIP commercial contract momentum will either justify the premium or hand the skeptics their argument. 

Until then, Wall Street’s $140 question has no answer.

PLTR Stock Price Activity: Palantir Technologies shares were up 6.67% at $152.90 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

articles.author: anusuya lahiri
articles.title: What's Going On With Palantir Stock Friday?
articles.teaser: Palantir (PLTR) stock jumps 3.98% to $149.04. Find out what's driving the latest rally and where analysts expect the stock to go next.
articles.body:
Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock traded higher on Friday as investors continued to favor artificial intelligence-driven technology stocks amid a broadly constructive market environment.

The Nasdaq gained 0.54%, while the S&P 500 rose 0.35%.

There was no major company-specific catalyst behind Friday’s move. Palantir appeared to benefit from sustained momentum in AI-related equities and improving investor risk appetite.

As one of the market’s most prominent AI software and data analytics companies, Palantir has become a frequent destination for investors seeking exposure to the enterprise AI theme.

The stock also outpaced the broader technology sector, which advanced 1.87%, suggesting buyers were actively accumulating Palantir shares rather than merely tracking sector-wide gains.

Enterprise AI Adoption Reinforces Bull Case

Sentiment around Palantir’s long-term growth story received an additional boost after its key partner, Snowflake Inc. (NYSE:SNOW), delivered stronger-than-expected quarterly results and highlighted accelerating enterprise AI adoption.

Snowflake’s commentary reinforced growing demand for data infrastructure and AI platforms, a trend that continues to support Palantir’s expansion across commercial and government markets.

Defense Opportunities Remain In Focus

Investors also reacted positively to reports that the U.S. government is preparing initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic drone infrastructure.

Given Palantir’s deep ties to U.S. defense and intelligence agencies, the development is viewed as a potential tailwind that could create additional contract opportunities over time.

Earnings And Analyst Outlook

The next major catalyst for Palantir is its expected Aug. 3, 2026, earnings report.

Analysts currently expect earnings of 33 cents per share, up from 16 cents a year earlier, on revenue of $1.81 billion versus $1.00 billion in the prior-year period.

Despite trading at a premium valuation of roughly 161 times earnings, Wall Street remains constructive on the stock. The consensus rating is Buy, with an average price forecast of $189.38. Recent analyst moves include:

  • Rosenblatt: Buy (Maintains forecast to $225.00) (May 21)
  • Citigroup: Buy (Raises forecast to $225.00) (May 6)
  • Argus Research: Upgraded to Buy (Forecast $190.00) (May 6)

Technical Analysis

From a trend perspective, PLTR is back in a more constructive near-term posture: it’s trading 11.4% above its 20-day SMA ($136.94) and 7.6% above its 50-day SMA ($141.72), which typically signals buyers are defending pullbacks faster. It’s also 3.5% above the 100-day SMA ($147.41), putting the stock just above a widely watched intermediate trend line.

The bigger-picture trend is still mixed because the stock remains 5.8% below its 200-day SMA ($161.94), and the 50-day SMA is still below the 200-day SMA (the “death cross” that occurred in February). In other words, the short-term rebound is real, but the longer-term trend repair isn’t fully complete until price can reclaim and hold above the longer moving average zone.

Momentum is improving on the MACD: it’s above its signal line and the histogram is positive, which points to fading downside pressure versus the prior downswing. For non-technical readers, MACD is a way to gauge whether momentum is strengthening or weakening by comparing a faster trend measure to a slower “signal” baseline.

Key levels are fairly clean here: bulls generally want to see follow-through toward the mid-$150s, while bears want to force the stock back into the prior breakdown area from April.

  • Key Resistance: $156.00 — a nearby round-number zone where rebounds can stall
  • Key Support: $128.50 — a prior demand area that lines up with a recent pivot zone after the April weakness

Price Action

PLTR Price Action: Palantir Technologies shares were up 3.98% at $149.04 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

articles.title: S&P 500 Hits Record Highs, Snowflake Jumps 37% On AI Boom: Stock Market Today
articles.teaser: U.S. stocks pushed to fresh record highs after a US-Iran ceasefire memorandum eased inflation fears, while Snowflake's 37% earnings blowout lifted AI software names.
articles.body:
U.S. stocks hit record highs Thursday after reports that Washington and Tehran agreed to a 60-day ceasefire extension and phased resumption of Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic.

The S&P 500 advanced 0.5% to a record 7,557.85, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 32 points, or 0.1%, to 50,676.

The Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.4% to a record 30,089. Within Magnificent Seven stocks, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) jumped 2.9%, while Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) edged 0.3% higher – on track to snap four straight sessions of losses.

The small-cap Russell 2000 rallied 0.6% to 2,937, the strongest performance among major U.S. benchmarks.

Read Also: Fed's Favorite Inflation Gauge Hits 3.8%, Highest Since May 2023

April PCE Report Delivered Mixed Read For Fed

Headline Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) inflation accelerated to 3.8% year-over-year – the hottest since early 2023 – with the monthly print up 0.4%, but core PCE rose just 0.2% on the month and 3.3% year-over-year, broadly in line with estimates.

Real personal spending grew just 0.1%, personal income was essentially flat, and first-quarter GDP was revised lower by 0.4 percentage points to 1.6% on softer investment, painting a picture of a consumer that is no longer outrunning prices.

The mixed macro print did little to soften the Fed’s hawkish chorus. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said rate hikes remain on the table if price pressures fail to converge back to the 2% target, echoing similar warnings from Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari.

Thursday’s Performance In Major US Indices

According to the Benzinga Pro platform:

  • The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:VOO) rose 0.5%.
  • The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA) edged 0.1% higher.
  • The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) gained 0.4%.
  • The iShares Russell 2000 ETF (NYSE:IWM) rallied 0.6%.

AI Software Spending Spree Lights Up Records Board

The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLK) led S&P 500 sectors with a 1.4% advance, fueled by a wave of AI software and infrastructure buying after Snowflake Inc. (NYSE:SNOW)‘s blowout print.

The data-cloud company rocketed 37% on its best session ever, after smashing both earnings and revenue estimates and and unveiling a $6 billion five-year commitment to expand its Amazon Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)‘s AWS infrastructure partnership.

Wall Street analysts flagged an “inflection” quarter for Snowflake, on the back of rising AI-cloud orders.

Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL) jumped 6%, Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) surged 5.7%, ServiceNow Inc. (NYSE:NOW) rallied 5.3% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) added 4.5%. 

At the other end, the Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLF) dropped 0.4% as Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) fell 1.7% and BlackRock Inc. (NYSE:BLK) shed 1.9%.

Industry ETFs amplified the risk-on tone. The Invesco WilderHill Clean Energy ETF (NYSE:PBW) jumped 2.0% as First Solar Inc. (NASDAQ:FSLR) rose 8.2%.

In retail, Best Buy Co. Inc. (NYSE:BBY) surged 18% after Q1 sales of $8.94 billion topped the $8.82 billion consensus, comparable sales rose 2% versus a 0.7% decline a year earlier, and management reiterated $6.45 in full-year adjusted EPS. 

Dollar Tree Inc. (NASDAQ:DLTR) climbed 17% after Q1 adjusted EPS of $1.74 beat the $1.55 consensus and the discounter lifted FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.70-$7.10.

Life-sciences leader Agilent Technologies Inc. (NYSE:A) jumped 17% after fiscal Q2 revenue of $1.83 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.49 beat estimates, with management raising the guidance on revenue.

Axon Enterprise Inc. (NASDAQ:AXON) rallied 13% after raising full-year revenue growth guidance to 30%-32% on a 700% year-over-year jump in AI-related product revenue and the disclosure of a $153 million long-term public safety contract.

On the downside, Everpure Inc. (NYSE:P) tumbled 12% as the data storage firm’s beat-and-raise was overshadowed by Q2 revenue guidance of $553 million, well below Wall Street’s projections.

Synopsys Inc. (NASDAQ:SNPS) slid 8.3% after fiscal Q2 revenue of $2.28 billion missed the $2.30 billion consensus by roughly $20 million despite a beat on EPS, with investors looking for a sharper guidance hike.

Salesforce Inc. (NYSE:CRM) dipped roughly 2% after the company beat on sales and EPS but offered Q2 revenue guidance slightly below consensus.
